# AGENTS.md: building an Annex app (node-web)

This folder is an **Annex app**: a small internal tool that runs behind the client's login on their Annex server. Read the contract with `annex contract` (or the `annex_contract` MCP tool; add a topic, e.g. `annex contract notify`, for email/Slack, webhooks, logging details or another stack) before making structural changes.

## The contract
<!-- contract:begin (generated by scripts/sync-contract.sh from toolkit/cli/src/annex_cli/contract.md; do not edit) -->
Contract version 2 (`ANNEX_CONTRACT_VERSION`). The contract is the authority: `annex contract` (MCP: `annex_contract`) prints the core, which this file only summarizes.
- Core sections: annex.yaml, Runtime rules, Cross-site requests, Injected environment, Gateway views (allowlist), Commands.
- Topics, fetched only when the app needs them: `annex contract notify` (sending email or Slack messages (notify:)); `annex contract webhooks` (receiving calls from Trello, Stripe, GitHub, Slack (webhooks:)); `annex contract logging` (the log format in detail, request ids, error grouping, browser errors, searching logs); `annex contract stack` (any language or framework without a template (Next.js, Streamlit, Django, Go...)).
<!-- contract:end -->

## What you may change
- `server.js` and any new modules, views or static files.
- `package.json` dependencies: pin exact versions (`"express": "5.3.0"`, no `^` or `~`).
- `annex.yaml`: `description`, `storage`, `data.views`, `notify`, `schedule` (with `type: web+job`), `env`, `secrets`.

## What you must not do
- **No login code.** The user is already signed in. Read them with `currentUser(req)` from `annex_runtime.js` (`.login`, `.name`, `.email`, `.groups`).
- **No database credentials and no direct product database access.** Product data comes only from `await gateway("<view>", {filters})`, for views listed under `data.views`. Your own data goes in Postgres via `DATABASE_URL` (set `storage.postgres: true`, add `pg` to dependencies), or in files under `/data` (set `storage.files: true`).
- **No Docker labels, ports or compose files.** Annex generates them.
- **No secrets in code, files or the image.** Declare the name under `secrets:` and ask a human to run `annex secret set <app> KEY`.
- **Don't change the Dockerfile's base image, `USER 10001` or `HEALTHCHECK`.** The app runs on a read-only filesystem; write only to `/tmp` and `/data`.

## Logging
Use `log` from `annex_runtime.js`, not `console.log()`: every line becomes one JSON object (`ts`, `level`, `msg` and your fields), which Annex stores and searches.
```js
import { log } from "./annex_runtime.js";
log.info("report written", { rows: 12, ms: 340 });
log.warn("gateway slow", { view: "<view>", ms: 2300 });
log.error("could not send", { status: e.status });
```
- **Pick the level:** `debug` detail for you (hidden unless `env: {LOG_LEVEL: debug}`), `info` what happened, `warn` odd but handled, `error` failed.
- `app.use(annexRequest)` in `server.js` gives every line of a request its `request_id` and `user`, and returns the `X-Request-Id` header. Keep it first.
- **Log errors with context** (what you were doing, which id), and counts instead of rows.
- **Never log** secrets, tokens, passwords, request bodies, cookies or full product records, or personal data beyond the user's login (log `matches=3`, not the search text).

## Errors
Errors are grouped for you: Annex reads the stored logs, and the first time a **new kind of error** shows up (a `log.error` line or an unhandled exception) the owner gets one email; more of the same are only counted. So:
- Log failures with `log.error(...)` (with the id or step you were on), not `log.info` or `console.log`; an error you handle and recover from is a `warn`.
- **Keep the browser part:** every page includes `<script src="/annex-errors.js"></script>` and `server.js` calls `mountBrowserErrors(app, express)`; together they report JavaScript errors the user hits as `source=browser` errors. Put the script tag in every page you add.

## Email and Slack
To email people or post to Slack, declare it in `annex.yaml` (`notify: {email: true, slack: ["#finance-reports"]}`) and use the helpers in `annex_runtime.js`. Never run an SMTP client or hold a Slack token of your own: Annex injects `ANNEX_OPS_URL` and a token that can do exactly what you declared.
```js
import { NotifyError, sendEmail, postSlack } from "./annex_runtime.js";
await sendEmail(["ana", "sam@annex.example"], "Report ready", { template: "notice",
  data: { title: "Report ready", body: "June is done.", link: "https://...", link_text: "Open" } });
await postSlack("#finance-reports", "Report ready: https://...");
```
- Recipients are logins (`"ana"`, as in `currentUser(req).login`) or company addresses. Anyone else is refused, and if one recipient is refused nothing is sent.
- Give `text`, `html` or `template="notice"`. **No attachments**: save the file under `/data` and email a link to it in your app.
- Limits: 60 emails and 60 Slack posts per hour per app. Slack only to the channels you declared.
- Failures throw `NotifyError` (`.status`, and a message that says what to fix). Decide whether a failed notification should fail your job.

## Rules the deploy checks
- Listen on `0.0.0.0:$PORT`, and make `GET /healthz` return 200 when ready.
- `name` is the hostname: lowercase letters, digits and `-`.
- Views must be in the gateway allowlist (see `annex contract`).
- **A job must exit non-zero when it fails**, so its owner is alerted (a job that catches its own error and exits 0 looks successful). Keep `/healthz` honest and fast: the owner is emailed when it fails.
- **Usage is counted for you** (signed-in page requests, not health checks or static files): nothing to add to the app. The owner sees totals on its discovery tile and in `annex usage`; never log or display other people's usage yourself.
- **Webhooks:** an endpoint declared under `webhooks:` must call `hook_event(headers)` first (`hookEvent(req)` in node; 401 on `HookError`), answer 2xx quickly, and dedupe by `event_id` (delivery is at least once). Give the provider `$ANNEX_HOOKS_URL/<name>`.

## Workflow
1. Edit the code. Test locally if you like: `npm install && PORT=8080 node server.js`. Identity headers and the gateway only exist on the server.
2. `annex deploy .` (or the `annex_deploy` MCP tool). Read any error, fix exactly what it names, and deploy again.
3. Open the URL it prints, then check `annex status <name>` and `annex logs <name>`.
